filtered_bits: bit 0 first segment hit, bit 1 second segment hit, bit 2 at least one first-segment candidate rejected by explicit filtering
limitations: Near=1 hit is exposed by widening to 0 and included by the explicit comparison, unlike direct RayQuery and translated 218 in this fixture.

A ray originating on the triangle yields t=0; native RayQuery does not expose that candidate with TMin=0 on either adapter. DXR requires nonnegative TMin and open triangle bounds, so using negative TMin is undefined.
The stacked case observes and rejects t=1 and accepts t=2; this tests continuation after candidate rejection, not general traversal order, all candidate tie cases, or full geometry/instance flags.

The control forces nonopaque candidates and commits them unconditionally after filtering. Opacity, culling, geometry/instance masks, Xbox hardware triangle arithmetic, invalid values, and the raw-SRV-to-native-TLAS binding are not proven.
